source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Allen campus publishes 77 MW of IT capacity, second among Texas facilities, but its compliance certifications and absent expansion plans make it a modest AI compute site.

The 77 MW is real and material, and at a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack it represents roughly 1,900 racks. It sits inside 976,000 square feet across three co-located buildings, DFW3 through DFW5, in the Dallas-Fort Worth metro. That metro has established power and fiber, but it is not among the largest AI cluster regions published to date.

The certifications point somewhere other than AI training. HIPAA, FISMA, PCI DSS, ISO 27001 and SSAE 16 Type II fit regulated healthcare, federal, payment and audited workloads, and they narrow the campus to tenants that need them. Large-scale AI training carries no standard compliance requirement, so this space is not aimed at it. Green Globes signals energy efficiency, which matters less when power is the binding constraint.

Texas is mapped to 133 data center sites and publishes capacity for fewer than one in seven of them, so the state's 475 MW published total is a floor rather than a full accounting. The 77 MW here is one campus within that partial picture. Nothing in the specifications states whether CyrusOne will repurpose compliance-oriented space for compute or build new unrestricted capacity at this location, and the suitability score of 76 lists announced expansion as the missing input. Address, coordinates and airport proximity are also unpublished, so the site's actual grid and network position cannot be judged from this data.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
